question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}3k \\ -6 \\ k \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that  $u⊥v.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =k\cdot 3k+1\cdot (-6)+3\cdot k+(-2)\cdot 0 \\  & =3{k}^{2}-6+3k+0 \\  & =3({k}^{2}+k-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3({k}^{2}+k-2) & =0 \\ 3(k+2)(k-1) & =0 \\ k & =-2,1.\end{aligned}
$$
